text:
maya_support: FYI - Vidly reporting sustained 5xx/504s to hosted inference since ~03:10 UTC. Customer says p95 requests are timing out, lots of tail timeouts. They included a sample trace id: trace-vidly-03.
prod-monitor-bot: ALERT: tenant=vidly, endpoint=/v1/generate, status=504, rate=7/min, continuous_batcher_queue_len=82, request_queue_depth=0.98, kv_cache_evictions=120/min
tom_oncall: assigning. Can you paste the raw error payloads + tenant config? also @sam_sre can you grab the batcher traces?
maya_support: paste below from customer: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_cust_vidly" -d '{"model":"rhino-7b-q4","input":"<doc long...>"}'` they said it fails after ~20s with 504.
sam_sre: checking metrics now. p95 gateway latency spiked to 28s, p99 ~42s. continuous_batcher_pending_requests metric hit 1200 on the host pool. request_queue_depth per-host hit the 0.98 throttle threshold and started early-rejects.
li_runtime: this looks like continuous batching backlog + KV-cache warmup. Model variant has big kv footprint; longseqs increase batch assembly time -> backlog. We should evict long requests and steer to smaller variant immediately.
maya_support: customer confirms they have some single requests ~6k tokens coming through via our hosted API.
sam_sre: runbook step A: throttle large sequences -> temp rule: reject >4096 tokens with 429 + Retry-After, or route to dedicated. Also runbook B: split traffic to rhino-3b-fallback.
li_runtime: commands to apply (on control plane):
```
# quick traffic split to fallback
redwoodctl routes update vidly --route /v1/generate --split '{"rhino-7b-q4":0.2,"rhino-3b":0.8}'
# set tenant config to reject longseqs
redwoodctl tenants patch vidly --set "max_input_tokens=4096"
```
sam_sre: applied monitoring check to auto-scale batcher concurrency and increased per-host batcher workers by +2 on the affected pool. Also temporarily bumped queue_depth_limit from 0.9 -> 0.98 (careful).
prod-monitor-bot: NOTE: autoscale event triggered at 03:24 UTC; batcher_workers increased. continuous_batcher_queue_len fell to 60 in 6m after split.

maya_support: relayed actions to customer. They still see some timeouts but rate decreasing.
jordan_csm: customer worried about billing for retries. suggested we waive charges for the spike window and send CM note.
tom_oncall: good mitigation. Next steps: 1) keep fallback split for 2 hours 2) add reject rule for >2048 tokens for hosted plans (policy review) 3) schedule eng-runtime follow-up to optimize kv-cache warmup for rhino-7b. @li_runtime please own follow-up.
li_runtime: will take. I'll instrument batch assembly latency per-seq-len and upload traces to the incident board. Also proposing a smart prefix cache warmup for common doc headers.
maya_support: Customer accepts temporary fix for now, asked to keep the channel updated. Closing when p99 < 10s for 30m.
prod-monitor-bot: p99 now 9.2s, continuous_batcher_queue_len 18, request_queue_depth 0.22
maya_support: thanks team :tada: — leaving open for 30m monitoring window.
deploy-bot: recent deploy: serving-runtime v2.14.1 at 02:58 UTC (no breaking changes).
tom_oncall: noted. If we see reoccurrence after fallback removal, we'll roll a targeted hotfix. I'll update the incident postmortem template and assign owners.
maya_support: closing thread when stable.
